subject.title: fix(plugin-sdk): update ssrf-runtime import path in cdp-proxy-bypass

question: Should the `ssrf-runtime-internal` Browser/Ollama helpers stay owner-scoped private, or should these SSRF/proxy-bypass helpers become public Plugin SDK exports?
rationale: Both repair directions can address the package-subpath failure, but exposing SSRF and managed-proxy bypass helpers changes the public SDK/security boundary and cannot be decided safely from code mechanics alone.

options.title: Preserve Owner-Scoped Access
options.body: Keep the helpers private and fix packaged Browser/Ollama resolution through the existing owner-scoped alias or staging path, with package lazy-load proof before merge.

options.title: Approve Public SDK Promotion
options.body: Land the public exports only with explicit SDK/security approval, docs/API metadata, replacement guardrails, and release-note context.

options.title: Choose A Canonical Replacement
options.body: Pause this branch if maintainers select a sibling PR or new replacement branch as the canonical fix for the same regression.

recommendation.title: Preserve Owner-Scoped Access
recommendation.body: Keep the helpers private and fix packaged Browser/Ollama resolution through the existing owner-scoped alias or staging path, with package lazy-load proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is primarily package/SDK boundary ownership, and this person authored the private SDK package hardening while also merging the relevant Browser/Ollama boundary PRs.
